originalTitle: THE GET BACK Trailer- Yella Beezy, Mo3 and Roy Lee (Short Film)
content: THE DEATH TRAP (Part 1) is a cinematic Dallas street drama about Roy Lee, MO3 and Yella Beezy, and the mentors who could have stopped it. In 2018, Dallas comedian Roy Lee (Roylee Pate) became the spark in one of the most talked-about feuds in Texas hip-hop. What started with words in Oak Cliff turned into a chain of events that took lives, changed families forever, and ended with no winners. This film follows that path, from Roy Lee's challenge and the comedy show that went wrong, to the shooting at Preston Valley, to Yella Beezy being shot on the Sam Rayburn Tollway, to MO3's death on I-35 in Dallas on November 11, 2020. Along the way, we sit with each man inside "The Inner Man," a one-on-one session where MO3 and Yella Beezy, in their own words from real interviews, reveal the boys behind the headlines: one who grew up with nothing, and one who lost his father as a child. On November 11, 2026, exactly six years after MO3's death, a Dallas County jury found Yella Beezy (Markies Conway) guilty of capital murder in the case, and he was sentenced to life without parole. His defense has disputed the state's case, and the case may continue on appeal. This film doesn't pick sides. It asks one question: what if someone had reached them first? Part 2 premieres November 27th. Subscribe and turn on notifications so you don't miss it. DISCLAIMER: THE DEATH TRAP is a dramatization made for storytelling, commentary, educational and entertainment purposes. Scenes in this film were created with AI and are reenactments, not real footage. Some characters, including the mentors and the children, are fictional or composites, and some dialogue and scenes are imagined, including the "what if" scenarios. Interview audio from MO3 and Yella Beezy comes from their own public interviews, used for commentary. Events involving shootings are depicted as reported by news outlets and public records; where facts were never confirmed, the film does not present them as fact, and no one is shown committing a crime that has not been established through legal proceedings. This film is not affiliated with or endorsed by the families or estates of anyone depicted. Our hearts go out to every family affected. If you or someone you know is caught up in street violence, please reach out to a local violence interruption program or a trusted mentor in your community.
